title: Test and close the fail-closed branch of the T-434 reset guard
description: T-434's reset guard fails closed when precedent.py cite --all exits outside {0,3} or raises while parsing, but no test forces that branch. It also fails OPEN on format drift: _precedent_task_citations skips any stdout line _CITE_ALL_LINE_RE does not match, so if cite --all changed its line format the scan would report zero hits, no problem, and reset would proceed. Today all 351 lines of the live output match the regex. Add the tests, and make an unrecognized nonempty line a problem (fail closed) without touching blackboard.py lines 522-575, which PR-063 cites byte-for-byte.
acceptance_criteria: A test forces precedent.py cite --all to exit 4 (write an unparseable PR-*.json into the temp root's precedents/) and asserts reset exits non-zero, logs board_reset_refused_citations with a non-null problem, and leaves the board and trash/ untouched.
A test asserts that the same exit-4 case proceeds only with --override-precedent-citations plus --note, and logs board_reset_citations_overridden with the problem string.

_precedent_task_citations treats any nonempty stdout line that does not match _CITE_ALL_LINE_RE as a problem (fail closed), with the offending line in the message; a test drives this branch (for example by pointing the scan at a stub that prints a drifted format, via a seam that does not change the default path).
The live-board check still passes: python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py cite --all on the real registry produces no unrecognized line, so reset behavior on the real repository is unchanged.
blackboard.py lines 522-575 are byte-identical before and after (record both sha256 values in the hand-off).
Full suite passes via goal_mode.py run; hand off to role verifier, never self-mark done.
